messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does:
  - BugCLI162Test.testInfiniteLoop creates a HelpFormatter, sets a very small width (20), and calls printHelp("app", options). The options include a -h/--help option with a long description (“This is a looooong description”). The test’s comment says “used to hang & crash”, i.e., it exercises the previously reported issue CLI-162.

- Where the wrapping happens:
  - printHelp(String, Options) delegates to printHelp(int, …) and then to printHelp(PrintWriter, int, …), which calls printOptions(...).
  - printOptions builds the formatted options line and delegates to renderOptions(...).
  - renderOptions computes:
    - the left padding (lpad),
    - the description padding (dpad),
    - the maximum width of the option prefix column (max),
    - then for each option creates the full line: lpad + option switches + dpad + description, and calls renderWrappedText(sb, width, nextLineTabStop, optBuf.toString()) with nextLineTabStop = max + descPad.

- The problematic loop:
  - renderWrappedText first finds a wrap position: pos = findWrapPos(text, width, 0).
  - If pos == -1, it appends the whole text and returns. Otherwise it appends text.substring(0, pos) and a newline, then enters a while(true) loop:
    - lastPos = pos
    - text = padding + text.substring(pos).trim() with padding = createPadding(nextLineTabStop)
    - pos = findWrapPos(text, width, 0)
    - If pos == -1, append the rest and return
    - If pos == lastPos, throw a RuntimeException “Text too long for line - … [CLI-162]”
    - Otherwise, append up to pos and continue

- How the bug manifests with a very small width:
  - With width set to 20, the label/prefix portion for an option (left pad + “-h,--help” + desc pad) can be longer than 20 characters. Consequently, the first call to findWrapPos(text, width, 0) finds a break inside the padding/prefix area instead of between content words.
  - After the first split, renderWrappedText rebuilds the line for the next iteration as “(nextLineTabStop spaces) + remainder”. Critically, nextLineTabStop = max + descPad is the indentation to align descriptions with the longest option label column. For a small overall width, nextLineTabStop can be greater than or very close to width.
  - Because the continuation line starts with padding whose length is greater than or equal to the allowed width, findWrapPos(text, width, 0) finds another wrap point inside that left padding again. That means the algorithm makes no progress towards consuming the actual description text.
  - Prior to the protective check, this repeated breaking within the left padding caused an infinite loop until an OutOfMemoryError, exactly as described in the current bug report (“infinite loop … until the JVM crashes”).
  - In the code shown, a guard was added: if (pos == lastPos) throw new RuntimeException to avoid the infinite loop. This prevents the hang but still causes the test to fail by raising an exception when width is too small for the indentation and at least one character of content cannot fit.

- Root cause:
  - The wrapping algorithm in renderWrappedText assumes that continuation lines have enough “effective width” left after nextLineTabStop spaces to print at least part of a word. When nextLineTabStop >= width, findWrapPos repeatedly returns a position inside the indentation, so progress stalls. The code tries to detect this by comparing pos to lastPos and throwing, but it doesn’t actually handle the situation gracefully.
  - Contributing detail: renderWrappedText always calls findWrapPos(text, width, 0) on the padded line, rather than wrapping within the content region (after the padding) or adjusting the effective width for continuation lines to width - nextLineTabStop.

- Why the test fails:
  - With width=20 and a long option prefix/indentation (nextLineTabStop), the formatter cannot place even one content character on a continuation line. The loop hits the guard and throws an exception to avoid the infinite loop; or, in versions without the guard, it loops indefinitely and crashes. Either way, the test that simply calls printHelp fails (by hang or by exception), demonstrating that the wrapping code does not robustly handle the case where nextLineTabStop >= width.

- Correct direction for a fix:
  - Ensure progress on continuation lines even when nextLineTabStop >= width:
    - Option A: cap nextLineTabStop to be less than width (e.g., min(nextLineTabStop, width - 1)).
    - Option B: compute and use an effective wrap width for continuation lines of at least 1 character (e.g., call findWrapPos on the content part with startPos = nextLineTabStop or adjust width to Math.max(width, nextLineTabStop + 1)).
    - Option C: if no character can fit after padding, bypass wrapping and append the remainder as-is on the same line, or split words at width boundaries rather than only on whitespace.
  - Any of these prevents the loop from repeatedly wrapping inside the left padding and eliminates the infinite loop/exception for very small widths.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(java.lang.StringBuffer, int, int, java.lang.String)
HelpFormatter.findWrapPos(java.lang.String, int, int)
HelpFormatter.renderOptions(java.lang.StringBuffer, int, org.apache.commons.cli.Options, int, int)
